title: Erb's Road shelter and homelessness plan funding
subtitle: Committee also received an employment pilot update, public health reports and the 2025 budget referral for chronic homelessness work.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that the Region keep funding and running the Erb's Road Hybrid Emergency Shelter until at least 2030, or as long as it is needed {{vote:m4}}. Staff will also ask Wilmot's Chief Building Official for a six-month extension on wastewater disposal while the shelter connects to existing Region-owned infrastructure. Staff said the shelter is on Regional land and that the holding tank is a temporary measure.

The committee also recommended endorsing the priorities and engagement approach in The Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, and referring the 2025 operating budget expansion to the strategic plan and budget process {{vote:m3}}. Staff stressed that the full estimated cost of the plan would not fall on Regional taxpayers and that other governments and partners would be approached.

Council still has to adopt these recommendations. The committee received for information an update on the employment services pilot, which is planned to end in March 2025, along with public health reports on seasonal illness and the dental program {{vote:m2}}. Funding decisions will come back through budget deliberations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended continuing to fund and coordinate the shelter until at least 2030 or as long as needed, and asking Wilmot's Chief Building Official for a six-month wastewater extension.
The committee recommended endorsing the plan's prioritization and engagement strategies and referring the 2025 operating budget expansion to the Regional strategic plan and budget process.
The committee received for information the seasonal illness report and the Public Health dental program update.

debate: Delegates from the shelter operator and a social development organization supported keeping Erb's Road open. They said it gives people a lockable cabin and supports, and that residents fear closure. One delegate noted residents' views on location differ: some value the rural setting, others want a site closer to downtown services.

Several councillors questioned the shelter's results. They noted that just under a fifth of residents have moved into permanent housing, and argued money should go to permanent supportive housing. Staff said this rate matches other programs, that about 40 of 50 residents are ready to move on if housing is available, and that closing the shelter would send some people back outdoors.

Neighbourhood safety was raised. Concerns included lighting and the lack of a sidewalk on the south side of Erb's Road, incidents affecting nearby businesses, and rural residents' security. Staff committed to look at lighting and sidewalks and to keep up neighbourhood meetings.

One councillor raised concerns about how the Region had handled permits and inspections during construction and about the wind-down planning. Staff said wind-down was not put in the report, citing the earlier closure of 84 Frederick as an example. They also said the sanitary connection would be on Regional land.

On the homelessness plan, councillors asked where the funding would come from and how to read the projection chart. Staff said they would not recommend the Region fund the whole estimated amount, and offered more detail at budget time and a data education session.
